headline: Public Law 114-5 directs Congress to award a Congressional Gold Medal to participants in the 1965 Selma to Montgomery voting rights marches.
what_it_does: The law tells the Speaker of the House and the President Pro Tempore of the Senate to arrange a presentation, on behalf of Congress, of a gold medal to the Foot Soldiers who took part in Bloody Sunday, Turnaround Tuesday, or the final Selma to Montgomery march in March 1965. The marches helped lead to the Voting Rights Act of 1965. The medals are national medals.
when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on March 7, 2015. The summary does not give a separate date for the medal presentation.
